public_rationale: Anthropic’s filing reports 80% consumption-based and 20% subscription-based recognized revenue for January–June 2026 [e1]. That half-year aggregate does not establish the annualized split for the four weeks ending April 6, 2026 [e1]. The filing also describes consumption billing for first-party applications, so consumption-based revenue cannot simply be equated with API revenue [e1]. This evidence neither confirms nor contradicts the estimated 75% API and 25% subscription split.
limitations: No matching early-April annualized API/subscription breakdown is supplied.
The available figures differ in period, measurement and category definitions.
Product-level revenue does not identify the billing-method split.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic's revenue is roughly 75% API and 25% subscriptions, by the author's estimate.

statement.excerpt: At this point, I estimate Anthropic’s revenue split to be more in the region of 75% API and 25% subscriptions, based on its supposed $2.5 billion in annualized revenue (out of $14 billion, so a little under 18%) in February coming from “Claude Code” (read: subscribers to Claude, there’s no “Claude Code” subscription).

from_speaker: in the region of 75% API and 25% subscriptions
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion concerns annualized revenue, so I assess the estimated split of the current run rate, rather than full-year recognized revenue.
For this ongoing observation, I use the latest reporting window identified in the supplied context: the four weeks ending April 6, 2026, with subscriptions measured at that date.
As an evaluator convention, approximately means within five percentage points of each stated share. No result should depend on this convention without being flagged.
API and subscription revenue must be classified by billing method. A product-level Claude Code total does not itself supply that classification.
criteria.support_condition: A comparable breakdown for the target reporting window places API revenue at approximately 75% and subscriptions at approximately 25%.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable breakdown places the shares materially outside that approximate range.
